clinician.trajectory_summary: A 10-day-old newborn presented with severe respiratory distress and reduced mobility in the left lower limb, with no history of trauma. An initial X-ray identified a mid-diaphyseal tibial fracture. Subsequent follow-up imaging, including X-rays at 2 and 8 months and a CT scan, revealed an absence of osseous consolidation of the fracture, along with characteristic features of congenital tibial pseudarthrosis (CPT). These features included discontinuities in the bone cortex, thickened cortex, irregularly distributed hypodense areas along the tibia, a curved fibula with a hypodensity, tibial erosion, significant antero-lateral fibular bowing, and a 1.5 cm leg length discrepancy. These imaging findings, combined with clinical and anamnestic data, led to the diagnosis of an osteodysplastic condition of the leg, specifically congenital tibial pseudarthrosis.
